facts.fact: RMS Titanic sank in April 1912 after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic.
Titanic carried lifeboats that could accommodate 1,178 people.
Inrushing water destroyed luxury interior spaces including the Grand Staircase.
Electric generators in the stern remained operational until the last few minutes.
Many passengers gathered on the rear poop deck for a last stand as the ship sank.
Water temperatures during the sinking were minus 2 degrees Celsius.
Plunging into freezing water causes cold shock with rapid gasping within 2 minutes.
Cold incapacitation prevents the use of limbs for swimming within 15 to 30 minutes.

sentences.text: What if you were on board the Titanic as it began to sink into the ocean?
In April 1912, the massive liner struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic.
You would soon learn that lifeboats could only save 1,178 people.
Inrushing water smashed through interior spaces like the Grand Staircase.
Electrical generators kept lights burning until the last few minutes.
You would retreat to the rear poop deck alongside hundreds of other passengers.
As the ship went under, you would plunge into minus 2 degrees Celsius water.
You would feel sudden cold shock, causing rapid gasping within 2 minutes.
Cold incapacitation would disable your limbs, leaving you unable to swim.
The sinking of the Titanic remains a tragic disaster in ocean history.
